**Commentary of Abu Hayyan (al-Bahr al-Muhit) on surah 78, verses 1–20 (part 1 of 2):**

[p. 409] Surat al-Naba' is Meccan and has forty-one verses.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿About what do they question one another? About the momentous news, about which they are in disagreement. No! They will come to know. Then, no! They will come to know.﴾ ﴿Have We not made the earth a resting place, and the mountains as pegs? And We created you in pairs, and made your sleep a rest, and made the night a covering, and made the day a time for livelihood. And We built above you seven strong heavens, and placed a blazing lamp, and sent down from the pressing clouds abundant water, that We may bring forth thereby grain and plants, and gardens of dense growth.﴾ ﴿Indeed, the Day of Decision is an appointed time, the Day when the Trumpet is blown and you come forth in multitudes, and the heaven is opened and becomes gateways, and the mountains are set in motion and become a mirage. Indeed, Hell has been lying in ambush, a dwelling place for the transgressors, abiding therein for ages. They will not taste therein any coolness or drink, except boiling water and dark, pus-like fluid, a fitting recompense. Indeed, they had not expected a reckoning, and they denied Our signs with complete denial. And We have recorded everything in a Book. So taste, for We shall increase you only in torment.﴾ ﴿Indeed, for the righteous is a place of success: gardens and vineyards, and maidens of equal age, and a full cup. They will not hear therein any idle talk or lying, as a recompense from your Lord, a gift by calculation, Lord of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them, the Most Gracious, none will have the power to address Him. On the Day when the Spirit and the angels stand in rows, none will speak except one whom the Most Gracious permits, and he will speak what is right. That is the true Day. So whoever wills may take a path to his Lord.﴾ ﴿Indeed, We have warned you of a near punishment, the Day when a man will see what his hands have sent forward, and the disbeliever will say, "Would that I were dust!"﴾

Al-subat: Ibn Qutayba said: its root meaning is "cutting" and "extending." Sleep is a cutting off of arduous occupations. From the sense of extending is the poet's saying:

"And if she extends it, it inclines in a long lock, as if it were the warp of women weaving with the hands of Khatham."

That is: if she extends her hair, it inclines and coils like the coiling of the warp in the hands of women who weave. Al-wahhaj: that which blazes and gleams. Al-mu'sir: al-Farra' said: the cloud that brings rain before it has gathered, like the young girl (al-jariya al-mu'sir) who has nearly reached menstruation but has not yet menstruated. Ibn Qutayba said similarly. Abu al-Najm al-'Ijli said:

"She walks slowly, her veil inclining, she has reached the age of puberty, or the time of her puberty has come near."

Al-thajj: Tha'lab said: its root meaning is intense pouring. Al-Azhari said: "matar thajjaj" means rain of intense pouring. One says "thajja al-ma'a" and "thajjtuhu thajjan wa thujuján," it is intransitive in the sense of pouring and transitive in the sense of pouring out. The poet, describing the rain, said:

"When she looks at it, there is a bent millstone-like cloud pouring out heavy rain of abundant downpours."

Alfafan: plural of laff, then laff was pluralized as alfaf. Al-kawa'ib: plural of kai'b, the woman whose breasts have protruded. From it comes "ka'b" of a man, due to its protrusion, and from it "al-Ka'ba." 'Asim ibn Qays al-Minqari said:

"How many a noble mare we have taken, and how many a maiden who knew not the pains of poverty, one who has reached puberty."

Al-dihaq: the full. It is derived from al-dahq, which is pressing and squeezing a thing with the hand, as if from its fullness it was pressed. It was also said: al-dihaq means successive. A poet said:

"A guest, 'Amir, came to us seeking hospitality, so we filled for him a cup to the brim."

Another said:

"You are closer to the heart than the thirsty one is to a brimming cup."

[p. 410] ﴿About what do they question one another? About the momentous news, about which they are in disagreement. No! They will come to know. Then, no! They will come to know. Have We not made the earth a resting place? And the mountains as pegs? And We created you in pairs, and made your sleep a rest, and made the night a covering, and made the day a time for livelihood. And We built above you seven strong heavens, and placed a blazing lamp, and sent down from the pressing clouds abundant water, that We may bring forth thereby grain and plants, and gardens of dense growth. Indeed, the Day of Decision is an appointed time, the Day when the Trumpet is blown and you come forth in multitudes, and the heaven is opened and becomes gateways, and the mountains are set in motion and become a mirage.﴾

This surah is Meccan. It is narrated that "when he (ﷺ) was sent as a prophet, the polytheists began to question one another, saying, 'What is it that he has brought?' and they disputed about what he had been sent with, so this was revealed." Its connection to what preceded it is clear: when He mentioned ﴿So in what statement after this will they believe?﴾ [al-Mursalat: 50], meaning after the statement which is the Qur'an, and they were disputing about it and questioning concerning it, He said: ﴿About what do they question one another?﴾

The majority read ﴿'amma﴾, while 'Abd Allah, Ubayy, 'Ikrima, and 'Isa read (ʿammā) with an alif, which is the original form of "ʿamma." The more common practice is to omit the alif of the interrogative "mā" when a preposition precedes it and it is attached to it. For retaining the alif, there is the poet's saying:

"For what he stood up, insulting me, a base man, like a pig rolling in ashes."

Al-Dahhak and Ibn Kathir, in one narration, read ʿammah with the heh of pause (hā' al-sakt), treating the connected reading as if it were a pause. This is because the more common practice when pausing on the interrogative "mā" is to add the heh of pause, except when it is followed by an attached word, in which case the heh is necessary in pausing, as in: "bi-ḥayyi mah?" (In which quarter?).

The interrogation about this carries exaltation, magnification, affirmation, and wonder, just as you say: "What a man Zayd is!" and "Zayd, what Zayd is!" As if, since he is unparalleled or nearly so, his kind was hidden from you, so you began to ask about him. Then the expression was stripped of magnifying the matter, and so it came in the Qur'an.

The pronoun in (yatasa'alun) refers to the people of Mecca. Then Allah, exalted is He, informed that they ﴿question one another about the momentous news﴾, which is the matter of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and what he brought of the Qur'an.

It was also said: the pronoun refers to the whole world, so the disagreement would be between the believer who affirms and the disbeliever who denies.

It was also said: what is questioned about is the Resurrection and the disagreement concerning it. ʿamma is connected to (yatasa'alun).

As for the one who reads ʿammah with the heh in connection, we have mentioned that it is treating the connected reading as a pause. [p. 411] ʿAn al-naba' is connected to an omitted verb, i.e., they question one another about the news.

Al-Zamakhshari permitted that he paused at ʿammah, then began with (yatasa'alun) "about the momentous news," on the basis that the verb is implicitly supplied for ʿammah, "they question one another," and it is omitted because what follows indicates it, like an ambiguous thing that is then explained.

Ibn 'Atiyya said: most grammarians said that His saying ﴿about the momentous news﴾ is connected to (yatasa'alun). The apparent meaning is as if He said: "Why do they question one another about the momentous news?"

Al-Zajjaj said: the statement is complete at His saying ﴿About what do they question one another?﴾ Then it would be expected that a respondent would answer and say: "They question one another about the news," so the conciseness and eloquence of the Qur'an required that the arguer hasten with the answer that the situation demands, and the juxtaposition is an argument and a hastening toward the point of their cutting off.

ʿAbd Allah and Ibn Jubayr read (yasā'alūna), without the tā' and with the sīn doubled, and its origin is (yatasā'alūna) with the tā' of address, and the second tā' was assimilated into the sīn.

(Kalla): a rebuke to those who question one another.

The majority read (with the yā' of the third person) in both. And from al-Dahhak: the first with the tā' in address, and the second with the yā' in the third person.

This repetition is an emphasis of the threat, and the omission of what knowledge relates to is for the sake of awe: that is, they will know what will befall them.

Then He, exalted is He, made them reflect upon His striking signs and the wonders of His creatures, which He originated from pure non-existence, and that reflection on these leads to faith in what the messengers brought of the Resurrection and the recompense. So He said: ﴿Have We not made the earth a resting place?﴾ He began with what they are constantly engaged with.

Al-mihad: the spread bedding. The majority read ﴿mihadan﴾. Mujahid, 'Isa, and some of the Kufans read (mahdan), with a fatha on the mīm and a sukūn on the hā'. Ibn 'Atiyya did not attribute this reading to 'Isa. Ibn Khalawayh said: "mahdan" in the singular: Mujahid and 'Isa al-Hamdani, who is al-Hawfi. So it is possible that the statement of Ibn 'Atiyya and "some of the Kufans" is a reference to 'Isa al-Hamdani. When they say "'Isa" without qualification, or "'Isa of Basra," he is 'Isa ibn 'Umar al-Thaqafi.

The discussion of al-mihad has preceded in al-Baqara at the beginning of the section ﴿And remember Allah﴾ [al-Baqara: 203].

﴿And the mountains as pegs﴾: that is, We fixed the earth with the mountains as a tent is fixed with pegs. Al-Afwah said:

"The house is not built except with pillars, and there is no support if the pegs are not driven in."

(Azwājan): that is, kinds of color, form, and language. Al-Zajjaj and others said: in pairs, male and female.

(Subatan): rest and tranquility. "Sabata al-rajul": he rested and left off work. Al-subat is a known ailment in which a person's silence is prolonged until he becomes deadly. Sleep resembles it except in harm. Qatada said: the sleeper is "masbut," who does not understand, as if he were dead.

(Libasan): that is, they cover themselves with it from eyes, in matters they do not want to appear. ﴿And made the day﴾: He set night against day, since in it is wakefulness.

﴿Ma'ashan﴾: a time of living, which is life, in which you go about your needs.

(Sab'an): that is, heavens. ﴿Shidadan﴾: firmly created, strong, not affected by the passing of ages except when Allah, mighty and majestic, wills. The poet said:

"When I came to him, he raised my station, and seated me upon the seven strong (heavens)."

(Sirajan): it is the sun. ﴿Wahhajan﴾: hot, blazing with intense flame. ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿUmar said: the sun is in the fourth heaven, its back toward us, and its flame blazes high.

﴿From the pressing clouds﴾: Ubayy, al-Hasan, Ibn Jubayr, Zayd ibn Aslam, Qatada, and Muqatil said: they are the heavens. Ibn 'Abbas, Abu al-'Aliya, al-Rabi', and al-Dahhak said: the clouds that pour, derived from 'asr (pressing), because the cloud is pressed and water comes out of it. It was also said: the clouds in which there is water but which have not yet rained. Ibn Kaysan said: they were so named from the point of their giving relief, so they are from al-'asra (relief), and from it is His saying: ﴿and therein they are given relief﴾ [Yusuf: 49]. The "'asir" is the one who gives relief, so it is a triliteral root. Here it came as "a'sara," meaning it entered the time of 'asr, so it became time for it to press. The form af'ala denotes entering into a thing.

Ibn 'Abbas also said, and Mujahid and Qatada: the winds, because they press the clouds. He attributed the sending down to them, since they were the cause of it. Ibn al-Zubayr, Ibn 'Abbas, al-Fadl ibn 'Abbas his brother, 'Abd Allah ibn Yazid, 'Ikrima, and Qatada read (bi-al-mu'sirat) with the bā' instead of min. Ibn 'Atiyya said: this strengthens that He meant the winds. Al-Zamakhshari said: there are two aspects: that what is meant is the winds that have come to press the clouds, and that what is meant is the clouds; because if the sending down is from them, it is through them, as you say: "He gave a dirham from his hand" and "He gave a dirham with his hand."

﴿Thajjajan﴾: poured out in abundance. From it is the best of the Hajj: 'ajj and thajj, that is, raising the voice in the talbiya and pouring out the blood of the sacrificial animal. Al-A'raj read (thajjahan) with a ḥā' at the end. Masajih al-ma' are its outlets, and water flows (yanthajih) in the valley.

﴿Grain and plants﴾: He began with grain because it is what one sustains oneself on, such as wheat and barley, and then followed with plants, which encompasses everything that grows of trees and herbage, and grain is included within it.

﴿Alfafan﴾: intertwined. Al-Zamakhshari said: it has no singular, like al-awza' and al-akhyaf. It was also said: its singular is laff. Sahib al-Iqlid said: al-Hasan ibn 'Ali al-Tusi recited to me:

"A garden, dense, and a luxurious life flowing, and companions, all of them fair, radiant."

If it were said that it is the plural of *multaffa* (a form with the extra letters removed), that would be a reasonable opinion. (End of quotation.) But there is no need for this view or for its reasonableness, since it has been mentioned in *al-Mufradat* (Mufradat al-Qur'an, by al-Raghib al-Isfahani) that its singular is *lifф* with a kasra on the *lam*, and that this is the view of the majority of the lexicographers. ﴿Indeed, the Day of Judgement (yawm al-fasl) is a day of decision.﴾ It is the Day of Resurrection, on which truth and falsehood will be separated. ﴿It was a appointed time (miqat).﴾ That is, in God's decree and judgement it is the time by which this world is fixed and at which it ends, or it is a limit for all creatures at which they stop. ﴿The Day the Trumpet (sur) is blown.﴾ This is a substitute (badal) for ﴿the Day of Decision﴾. Al-Zamakhshari said: "Or it is an explanatory apposition (atf bayan)." The discussion of the *sur* has already been covered. Abu 'Iyad read (fi al-suwar) with a fatha on the *waw*, as the plural of *surah*, meaning that God returns the spirits to the bodies. The majority read it with a sukun on the *waw*. ﴿And you will come (fa-ta'tun)﴾ from the graves to the place of standing in groups (umam), each community with its leader (imam). It was also said: in differing groups. Al-Zamakhshari mentioned a hadith about hideous conditions for ten categories of people who will be created in those states, and the cause of creating those who are created in that condition. God knows best its authenticity.

The Kufans read (wa-futihat) with a light *fa'* (khaff), while the majority read it with the emphatic *fa'* (tashdid). ﴿So it will be gates (abwaban)﴾: it will be split open until there are openings in it like gates in walls. It was also said: it will be broken into small pieces until it becomes like tablets, the familiar gates. Al-Zamakhshari said: "(It will be opened so it becomes gates): that is, its gates will be many because of the descent of the angels, as if it is nothing but open gates, like His saying: ﴿And We caused the earth to burst forth with springs﴾ [al-Qamar: 12], as if all of it were springs gushing forth." It was also said: the gates are the roads and paths, meaning it will be removed and the place will open up and become roads that nothing can block. ﴿So it will become a mirage (sarab)﴾: that is, it will become something like nothing, due to the scattering of its parts and the dispersal of its substances. End of quotation. Ibn 'Atiyya said: it is an expression for its dissolving and perishing after becoming scattered dust, and he did not intend that the mountains resemble water to a viewer at a distance. Al-Wahidi said: it is by omission of a modifier, meaning "possessing gates."

That is: if she extends her hair, it inclines and coils like the coiling of the warp in the hands of women who weave. Al-wahhaj: that which blazes and gleams. "A garden, dense, and a luxurious life flowing, and companions, all of them fair, radiant."

But there is no need for this view or for its reasonableness, since it has been mentioned in *al-Mufradat* (Mufradat al-Qur'an, by al-Raghib al-Isfahani) that its singular is *lifф* with a kasra on the *lam*, and that this is the view of the majority of the lexicographers. ﴿Indeed, the Day of Judgement (yawm al-fasl) is a day of decision.﴾ It is the Day of Resurrection, on which truth and falsehood will be separated. ﴿It was a appointed time (miqat).﴾ That is, in God's decree and judgement it is the time by which this world is fixed and at which it ends, or it is a limit for all creatures at which they stop. ﴿The Day the Trumpet (sur) is blown.﴾ This is a substitute (badal) for ﴿the Day of Decision﴾. Al-Zamakhshari said: "Or it is an explanatory apposition (atf bayan)." The discussion of the *sur* has already been covered. Abu 'Iyad read (fi al-suwar) with a fatha on the *waw*, as the plural of *surah*, meaning that God returns the spirits to the bodies. The majority read it with a sukun on the *waw*. ﴿And you will come (fa-ta'tun)﴾ from the graves to the place of standing in groups (umam), each community with its leader (imam). It was also said: in differing groups. Al-Zamakhshari mentioned a hadith about hideous conditions for ten categories of people who will be created in those states, and the cause of creating those who are created in that condition. God knows best its authenticity.

The Kufans read (wa-futihat) with a light *fa'* (khaff), while the majority read it with the emphatic *fa'* (tashdid). ﴿So it will be gates (abwaban)﴾: it will be split open until there are openings in it like gates in walls. It was also said: it will be broken into small pieces until it becomes like tablets, the familiar gates. Al-Zamakhshari said: "(It will be opened so it becomes gates): that is, its gates will be many because of the descent of the angels, as if it is nothing but open gates, like His saying: ﴿And We caused the earth to burst forth with springs﴾ [al-Qamar: 12], as if all of it were springs gushing forth." It was also said: the gates are the roads and paths, meaning it will be removed and the place will open up and become roads that nothing can block. ﴿So it will become a mirage (sarab)﴾: that is, it will become something like nothing, due to the scattering of its parts and the dispersal of its substances. End of quotation. Ibn 'Atiyya said: it is an expression for its dissolving and perishing after becoming scattered dust, and he did not intend that the mountains resemble water to a viewer at a distance. Al-Wahidi said: it is by omission of a modifier, meaning "possessing gates."

This repetition is an emphasis of the threat, and the omission of what knowledge relates to is for the sake of awe: that is, they will know what will befall them.

(Libasan): that is, they cover themselves with it from eyes, in matters they do not want to appear. ﴿And made the day﴾: He set night against day, since in it is wakefulness.

(Sab'an): that is, heavens. ﴿Shidadan﴾: firmly created, strong, not affected by the passing of ages except when Allah, mighty and majestic, wills. The poet said:

It was also said: in differing groups. Al-Zamakhshari mentioned a hadith about hideous conditions for ten categories of people who will be created in those states, and the cause of creating those who are created in that condition. God knows best its authenticity.

The Kufans read (wa-futihat) with a light *fa'* (khaff), while the majority read it with the emphatic *fa'* (tashdid). ﴿So it will be gates (abwaban)﴾: it will be split open until there are openings in it like gates in walls. It was also said: it will be broken into small pieces until it becomes like tablets, the familiar gates. Al-Zamakhshari said: "(It will be opened so it becomes gates): that is, its gates will be many because of the descent of the angels, as if it is nothing but open gates, like His saying: ﴿And We caused the earth to burst forth with springs﴾ [al-Qamar: 12], as if all of it were springs gushing forth." It was also said: the gates are the roads and paths, meaning it will be removed and the place will open up and become roads that nothing can block. ﴿So it will become a mirage (sarab)﴾: that is, it will become something like nothing, due to the scattering of its parts and the dispersal of its substances. End of quotation. Ibn 'Atiyya said: it is an expression for its dissolving and perishing after becoming scattered dust, and he did not intend that the mountains resemble water to a viewer at a distance. Al-Wahidi said: it is by omission of a modifier, meaning "possessing gates."

(Libasan): that is, they cover themselves with it from eyes, in matters they do not want to appear. ﴿And made the day﴾: He set night against day, since in it is wakefulness.

(Sab'an): that is, heavens. ﴿Shidadan﴾: firmly created, strong, not affected by the passing of ages except when Allah, mighty and majestic, wills. The poet said:

That is: if she extends her hair, it inclines and coils like the coiling of the warp in the hands of women who weave. Al-wahhaj: that which blazes and gleams. ﴿And the mountains as pegs﴾: that is, We fixed the earth with the mountains as a tent is fixed with pegs. Al-Afwah said:

"The house is not built except with pillars, and there is no support if the pegs are not driven in."

(Azwājan): that is, kinds of color, form, and language. Al-Zajjaj and others said: in pairs, male and female.

(Libasan): that is, they cover themselves with it from eyes, in matters they do not want to appear. ﴿And made the day﴾: He set night against day, since in it is wakefulness.

﴿Ma'ashan﴾: a time of living, which is life, in which you go about your needs.

(Sab'an): that is, heavens. ﴿Shidadan﴾: firmly created, strong, not affected by the passing of ages except when Allah, mighty and majestic, wills. The poet said:

"When I came to him, he raised my station, and seated me upon the seven strong (heavens)."

It was also said: the clouds in which there is water but which have not yet rained. ﴿Grain and plants﴾: He began with grain because it is what one sustains oneself on, such as wheat and barley, and then followed with plants, which encompasses everything that grows of trees and herbage, and grain is included within it.

"A garden, dense, and a luxurious life flowing, and companions, all of them fair, radiant."

But there is no need for this view or for its reasonableness, since it has been mentioned in *al-Mufradat* (Mufradat al-Qur'an, by al-Raghib al-Isfahani) that its singular is *lifф* with a kasra on the *lam*, and that this is the view of the majority of the lexicographers. ﴿Indeed, the Day of Judgement (yawm al-fasl) is a day of decision.﴾ It is the Day of Resurrection, on which truth and falsehood will be separated. ﴿It was a appointed time (miqat).﴾ That is, in God's decree and judgement it is the time by which this world is fixed and at which it ends, or it is a limit for all creatures at which they stop. ﴿The Day the Trumpet (sur) is blown.﴾ This is a substitute (badal) for ﴿the Day of Decision﴾. Al-Zamakhshari said: "Or it is an explanatory apposition (atf bayan)." The discussion of the *sur* has already been covered. Abu 'Iyad read (fi al-suwar) with a fatha on the *waw*, as the plural of *surah*, meaning that God returns the spirits to the bodies. The majority read it with a sukun on the *waw*. ﴿And you will come (fa-ta'tun)﴾ from the graves to the place of standing in groups (umam), each community with its leader (imam). It was also said: in differing groups. Al-Zamakhshari mentioned a hadith about hideous conditions for ten categories of people who will be created in those states, and the cause of creating those who are created in that condition. God knows best its authenticity.

The Kufans read (wa-futihat) with a light *fa'* (khaff), while the majority read it with the emphatic *fa'* (tashdid). ﴿So it will be gates (abwaban)﴾: it will be split open until there are openings in it like gates in walls. It was also said: it will be broken into small pieces until it becomes like tablets, the familiar gates. Al-Zamakhshari said: "(It will be opened so it becomes gates): that is, its gates will be many because of the descent of the angels, as if it is nothing but open gates, like His saying: ﴿And We caused the earth to burst forth with springs﴾ [al-Qamar: 12], as if all of it were springs gushing forth." It was also said: the gates are the roads and paths, meaning it will be removed and the place will open up and become roads that nothing can block. ﴿So it will become a mirage (sarab)﴾: that is, it will become something like nothing, due to the scattering of its parts and the dispersal of its substances. End of quotation. Ibn 'Atiyya said: it is an expression for its dissolving and perishing after becoming scattered dust, and he did not intend that the mountains resemble water to a viewer at a distance. Al-Wahidi said: it is by omission of a modifier, meaning "possessing gates."

Ibn 'Abbas also said, and Mujahid and Qatada: the winds, because they press the clouds. He attributed the sending down to them, since they were the cause of it. Ibn al-Zubayr, Ibn 'Abbas, al-Fadl ibn 'Abbas his brother, 'Abd Allah ibn Yazid, 'Ikrima, and Qatada read (bi-al-mu'sirat) with the bā' instead of min. Ibn 'Atiyya said: this strengthens that He meant the winds. Al-Zamakhshari said: there are two aspects: that what is meant is the winds that have come to press the clouds, and that what is meant is the clouds; because if the sending down is from them, it is through them, as you say: "He gave a dirham from his hand" and "He gave a dirham with his hand."

﴿Thajjajan﴾: poured out in abundance. From it is the best of the Hajj: 'ajj and thajj, that is, raising the voice in the talbiya and pouring out the blood of the sacrificial animal. Al-A'raj read (thajjahan) with a ḥā' at the end. Masajih al-ma' are its outlets, and water flows (yanthajih) in the valley.

﴿Grain and plants﴾: He began with grain because it is what one sustains oneself on, such as wheat and barley, and then followed with plants, which encompasses everything that grows of trees and herbage, and grain is included within it.

﴿Alfafan﴾: intertwined. Al-Zamakhshari said: it has no singular, like al-awza' and al-akhyaf. It was also said: its singular is laff. Sahib al-Iqlid said: al-Hasan ibn 'Ali al-Tusi recited to me:

"A garden, dense, and a luxurious life flowing, and companions, all of them fair, radiant."

If it were said that it is the plural of *multaffa* (a form with the extra letters removed), that would be a reasonable opinion. (End of quotation.) But there is no need for this view or for its reasonableness, since it has been mentioned in *al-Mufradat* (Mufradat al-Qur'an, by al-Raghib al-Isfahani) that its singular is *lifф* with a kasra on the *lam*, and that this is the view of the majority of the lexicographers. ﴿Indeed, the Day of Judgement (yawm al-fasl) is a day of decision.﴾ It is the Day of Resurrection, on which truth and falsehood will be separated. ﴿It was a appointed time (miqat).﴾ That is, in God's decree and judgement it is the time by which this world is fixed and at which it ends, or it is a limit for all creatures at which they stop. ﴿The Day the Trumpet (sur) is blown.﴾ This is a substitute (badal) for ﴿the Day of Decision﴾. Al-Zamakhshari said: "Or it is an explanatory apposition (atf bayan)." The discussion of the *sur* has already been covered. Abu 'Iyad read (fi al-suwar) with a fatha on the *waw*, as the plural of *surah*, meaning that God returns the spirits to the bodies. The majority read it with a sukun on the *waw*. ﴿And you will come (fa-ta'tun)﴾ from the graves to the place of standing in groups (umam), each community with its leader (imam). It was also said: in differing groups. Al-Zamakhshari mentioned a hadith about hideous conditions for ten categories of people who will be created in those states, and the cause of creating those who are created in that condition. God knows best its authenticity.

The Kufans read (wa-futihat) with a light *fa'* (khaff), while the majority read it with the emphatic *fa'* (tashdid). ﴿So it will be gates (abwaban)﴾: it will be split open until there are openings in it like gates in walls. It was also said: it will be broken into small pieces until it becomes like tablets, the familiar gates. Al-Zamakhshari said: "(It will be opened so it becomes gates): that is, its gates will be many because of the descent of the angels, as if it is nothing but open gates, like His saying: ﴿And We caused the earth to burst forth with springs﴾ [al-Qamar: 12], as if all of it were springs gushing forth." It was also said: the gates are the roads and paths, meaning it will be removed and the place will open up and become roads that nothing can block. ﴿So it will become a mirage (sarab)﴾: that is, it will become something like nothing, due to the scattering of its parts and the dispersal of its substances. End of quotation. Ibn 'Atiyya said: it is an expression for its dissolving and perishing after becoming scattered dust, and he did not intend that the mountains resemble water to a viewer at a distance. Al-Wahidi said: it is by omission of a modifier, meaning "possessing gates."

**Commentary of Abu Hayyan (al-Bahr al-Muhit) on surah 78, verses 1–20 (part 1 of 2):**

[p. 409] Surat al-Naba' is Meccan and has forty-one verses.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿About what do they question one another? About the momentous news, about which they are in disagreement. No! They will come to know. Then, no! They will come to know.﴾ ﴿Have We not made the earth a resting place, and the mountains as pegs? And We created you in pairs, and made your sleep a rest, and made the night a covering, and made the day a time for livelihood. And We built above you seven strong heavens, and placed a blazing lamp, and sent down from the pressing clouds abundant water, that We may bring forth thereby grain and plants, and gardens of dense growth.﴾ ﴿Indeed, the Day of Decision is an appointed time, the Day when the Trumpet is blown and you come forth in multitudes, and the heaven is opened and becomes gateways, and the mountains are set in motion and become a mirage. Indeed, Hell has been lying in ambush, a dwelling place for the transgressors, abiding therein for ages. They will not taste therein any coolness or drink, except boiling water and dark, pus-like fluid, a fitting recompense. Indeed, they had not expected a reckoning, and they denied Our signs with complete denial. And We have recorded everything in a Book. So taste, for We shall increase you only in torment.﴾ ﴿Indeed, for the righteous is a place of success: gardens and vineyards, and maidens of equal age, and a full cup. They will not hear therein any idle talk or lying, as a recompense from your Lord, a gift by calculation, Lord of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them, the Most Gracious, none will have the power to address Him. On the Day when the Spirit and the angels stand in rows, none will speak except one whom the Most Gracious permits, and he will speak what is right. That is the true Day. So whoever wills may take a path to his Lord.﴾ ﴿Indeed, We have warned you of a near punishment, the Day when a man will see what his hands have sent forward, and the disbeliever will say, "Would that I were dust!"﴾

Al-subat: Ibn Qutayba said: its root meaning is "cutting" and "extending." Sleep is a cutting off of arduous occupations. From the sense of extending is the poet's saying:

"And if she extends it, it inclines in a long lock, as if it were the warp of women weaving with the hands of Khatham."

That is: if she extends her hair, it inclines and coils like the coiling of the warp in the hands of women who weave. Al-wahhaj: that which blazes and gleams. Al-mu'sir: al-Farra' said: the cloud that brings rain before it has gathered, like the young girl (al-jariya al-mu'sir) who has nearly reached menstruation but has not yet menstruated. Ibn Qutayba said similarly. Abu al-Najm al-'Ijli said:

"She walks slowly, her veil inclining, she has reached the age of puberty, or the time of her puberty has come near."

Al-thajj: Tha'lab said: its root meaning is intense pouring. Al-Azhari said: "matar thajjaj" means rain of intense pouring. One says "thajja al-ma'a" and "thajjtuhu thajjan wa thujuján," it is intransitive in the sense of pouring and transitive in the sense of pouring out. The poet, describing the rain, said:

"When she looks at it, there is a bent millstone-like cloud pouring out heavy rain of abundant downpours."

Alfafan: plural of laff, then laff was pluralized as alfaf. Al-kawa'ib: plural of kai'b, the woman whose breasts have protruded. From it comes "ka'b" of a man, due to its protrusion, and from it "al-Ka'ba." 'Asim ibn Qays al-Minqari said:

"How many a noble mare we have taken, and how many a maiden who knew not the pains of poverty, one who has reached puberty."

Al-dihaq: the full. It is derived from al-dahq, which is pressing and squeezing a thing with the hand, as if from its fullness it was pressed. It was also said: al-dihaq means successive. A poet said:

"A guest, 'Amir, came to us seeking hospitality, so we filled for him a cup to the brim."

Another said:

"You are closer to the heart than the thirsty one is to a brimming cup."

[p. 410] ﴿About what do they question one another? About the momentous news, about which they are in disagreement. No! They will come to know. Then, no! They will come to know. Have We not made the earth a resting place? And the mountains as pegs? And We created you in pairs, and made your sleep a rest, and made the night a covering, and made the day a time for livelihood. And We built above you seven strong heavens, and placed a blazing lamp, and sent down from the pressing clouds abundant water, that We may bring forth thereby grain and plants, and gardens of dense growth. Indeed, the Day of Decision is an appointed time, the Day when the Trumpet is blown and you come forth in multitudes, and the heaven is opened and becomes gateways, and the mountains are set in motion and become a mirage.﴾

This surah is Meccan. It is narrated that "when he (ﷺ) was sent as a prophet, the polytheists began to question one another, saying, 'What is it that he has brought?' and they disputed about what he had been sent with, so this was revealed." Its connection to what preceded it is clear: when He mentioned ﴿So in what statement after this will they believe?﴾ [al-Mursalat: 50], meaning after the statement which is the Qur'an, and they were disputing about it and questioning concerning it, He said: ﴿About what do they question one another?﴾

The majority read ﴿'amma﴾, while 'Abd Allah, Ubayy, 'Ikrima, and 'Isa read (ʿammā) with an alif, which is the original form of "ʿamma." The more common practice is to omit the alif of the interrogative "mā" when a preposition precedes it and it is attached to it. For retaining the alif, there is the poet's saying:

"For what he stood up, insulting me, a base man, like a pig rolling in ashes."

Al-Dahhak and Ibn Kathir, in one narration, read ʿammah with the heh of pause (hā' al-sakt), treating the connected reading as if it were a pause. This is because the more common practice when pausing on the interrogative "mā" is to add the heh of pause, except when it is followed by an attached word, in which case the heh is necessary in pausing, as in: "bi-ḥayyi mah?" (In which quarter?).

The interrogation about this carries exaltation, magnification, affirmation, and wonder, just as you say: "What a man Zayd is!" and "Zayd, what Zayd is!" As if, since he is unparalleled or nearly so, his kind was hidden from you, so you began to ask about him. Then the expression was stripped of magnifying the matter, and so it came in the Qur'an.

The pronoun in (yatasa'alun) refers to the people of Mecca. Then Allah, exalted is He, informed that they ﴿question one another about the momentous news﴾, which is the matter of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and what he brought of the Qur'an.

It was also said: the pronoun refers to the whole world, so the disagreement would be between the believer who affirms and the disbeliever who denies.

It was also said: what is questioned about is the Resurrection and the disagreement concerning it. ʿamma is connected to (yatasa'alun).

As for the one who reads ʿammah with the heh in connection, we have mentioned that it is treating the connected reading as a pause. [p. 411] ʿAn al-naba' is connected to an omitted verb, i.e., they question one another about the news.

Al-Zamakhshari permitted that he paused at ʿammah, then began with (yatasa'alun) "about the momentous news," on the basis that the verb is implicitly supplied for ʿammah, "they question one another," and it is omitted because what follows indicates it, like an ambiguous thing that is then explained.

Ibn 'Atiyya said: most grammarians said that His saying ﴿about the momentous news﴾ is connected to (yatasa'alun). The apparent meaning is as if He said: "Why do they question one another about the momentous news?"

Al-Zajjaj said: the statement is complete at His saying ﴿About what do they question one another?﴾ Then it would be expected that a respondent would answer and say: "They question one another about the news," so the conciseness and eloquence of the Qur'an required that the arguer hasten with the answer that the situation demands, and the juxtaposition is an argument and a hastening toward the point of their cutting off.

ʿAbd Allah and Ibn Jubayr read (yasā'alūna), without the tā' and with the sīn doubled, and its origin is (yatasā'alūna) with the tā' of address, and the second tā' was assimilated into the sīn.

(Kalla): a rebuke to those who question one another.

The majority read (with the yā' of the third person) in both. And from al-Dahhak: the first with the tā' in address, and the second with the yā' in the third person.

This repetition is an emphasis of the threat, and the omission of what knowledge relates to is for the sake of awe: that is, they will know what will befall them.

Then He, exalted is He, made them reflect upon His striking signs and the wonders of His creatures, which He originated from pure non-existence, and that reflection on these leads to faith in what the messengers brought of the Resurrection and the recompense. So He said: ﴿Have We not made the earth a resting place?﴾ He began with what they are constantly engaged with.

Al-mihad: the spread bedding. The majority read ﴿mihadan﴾. Mujahid, 'Isa, and some of the Kufans read (mahdan), with a fatha on the mīm and a sukūn on the hā'. Ibn 'Atiyya did not attribute this reading to 'Isa. Ibn Khalawayh said: "mahdan" in the singular: Mujahid and 'Isa al-Hamdani, who is al-Hawfi. So it is possible that the statement of Ibn 'Atiyya and "some of the Kufans" is a reference to 'Isa al-Hamdani. When they say "'Isa" without qualification, or "'Isa of Basra," he is 'Isa ibn 'Umar al-Thaqafi.

The discussion of al-mihad has preceded in al-Baqara at the beginning of the section ﴿And remember Allah﴾ [al-Baqara: 203].

﴿And the mountains as pegs﴾: that is, We fixed the earth with the mountains as a tent is fixed with pegs. Al-Afwah said:

"The house is not built except with pillars, and there is no support if the pegs are not driven in."

(Azwājan): that is, kinds of color, form, and language. Al-Zajjaj and others said: in pairs, male and female.

(Subatan): rest and tranquility. "Sabata al-rajul": he rested and left off work. Al-subat is a known ailment in which a person's silence is prolonged until he becomes deadly. Sleep resembles it except in harm. Qatada said: the sleeper is "masbut," who does not understand, as if he were dead.

(Libasan): that is, they cover themselves with it from eyes, in matters they do not want to appear. ﴿And made the day﴾: He set night against day, since in it is wakefulness.

﴿Ma'ashan﴾: a time of living, which is life, in which you go about your needs.

(Sab'an): that is, heavens. ﴿Shidadan﴾: firmly created, strong, not affected by the passing of ages except when Allah, mighty and majestic, wills. The poet said:

"When I came to him, he raised my station, and seated me upon the seven strong (heavens)."

(Sirajan): it is the sun. ﴿Wahhajan﴾: hot, blazing with intense flame. ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿUmar said: the sun is in the fourth heaven, its back toward us, and its flame blazes high.

﴿From the pressing clouds﴾: Ubayy, al-Hasan, Ibn Jubayr, Zayd ibn Aslam, Qatada, and Muqatil said: they are the heavens. Ibn 'Abbas, Abu al-'Aliya, al-Rabi', and al-Dahhak said: the clouds that pour, derived from 'asr (pressing), because the cloud is pressed and water comes out of it. It was also said: the clouds in which there is water but which have not yet rained. Ibn Kaysan said: they were so named from the point of their giving relief, so they are from al-'asra (relief), and from it is His saying: ﴿and therein they are given relief﴾ [Yusuf: 49]. The "'asir" is the one who gives relief, so it is a triliteral root. Here it came as "a'sara," meaning it entered the time of 'asr, so it became time for it to press. The form af'ala denotes entering into a thing.

Ibn 'Abbas also said, and Mujahid and Qatada: the winds, because they press the clouds. He attributed the sending down to them, since they were the cause of it. Ibn al-Zubayr, Ibn 'Abbas, al-Fadl ibn 'Abbas his brother, 'Abd Allah ibn Yazid, 'Ikrima, and Qatada read (bi-al-mu'sirat) with the bā' instead of min. Ibn 'Atiyya said: this strengthens that He meant the winds. Al-Zamakhshari said: there are two aspects: that what is meant is the winds that have come to press the clouds, and that what is meant is the clouds; because if the sending down is from them, it is through them, as you say: "He gave a dirham from his hand" and "He gave a dirham with his hand."

﴿Thajjajan﴾: poured out in abundance. From it is the best of the Hajj: 'ajj and thajj, that is, raising the voice in the talbiya and pouring out the blood of the sacrificial animal. Al-A'raj read (thajjahan) with a ḥā' at the end. Masajih al-ma' are its outlets, and water flows (yanthajih) in the valley.

﴿Grain and plants﴾: He began with grain because it is what one sustains oneself on, such as wheat and barley, and then followed with plants, which encompasses everything that grows of trees and herbage, and grain is included within it.

﴿Alfafan﴾: intertwined. Al-Zamakhshari said: it has no singular, like al-awza' and al-akhyaf. It was also said: its singular is laff. Sahib al-Iqlid said: al-Hasan ibn 'Ali al-Tusi recited to me:

"A garden, dense, and a luxurious life flowing, and companions, all of them fair, radiant."

If it were said that it is the plural of *multaffa* (a form with the extra letters removed), that would be a reasonable opinion. (End of quotation.) But there is no need for this view or for its reasonableness, since it has been mentioned in *al-Mufradat* (Mufradat al-Qur'an, by al-Raghib al-Isfahani) that its singular is *lifф* with a kasra on the *lam*, and that this is the view of the majority of the lexicographers. ﴿Indeed, the Day of Judgement (yawm al-fasl) is a day of decision.﴾ It is the Day of Resurrection, on which truth and falsehood will be separated. ﴿It was a appointed time (miqat).﴾ That is, in God's decree and judgement it is the time by which this world is fixed and at which it ends, or it is a limit for all creatures at which they stop. ﴿The Day the Trumpet (sur) is blown.﴾ This is a substitute (badal) for ﴿the Day of Decision﴾. Al-Zamakhshari said: "Or it is an explanatory apposition (atf bayan)." The discussion of the *sur* has already been covered. Abu 'Iyad read (fi al-suwar) with a fatha on the *waw*, as the plural of *surah*, meaning that God returns the spirits to the bodies. The majority read it with a sukun on the *waw*. ﴿And you will come (fa-ta'tun)﴾ from the graves to the place of standing in groups (umam), each community with its leader (imam). It was also said: in differing groups. Al-Zamakhshari mentioned a hadith about hideous conditions for ten categories of people who will be created in those states, and the cause of creating those who are created in that condition. God knows best its authenticity.

The Kufans read (wa-futihat) with a light *fa'* (khaff), while the majority read it with the emphatic *fa'* (tashdid). ﴿So it will be gates (abwaban)﴾: it will be split open until there are openings in it like gates in walls. It was also said: it will be broken into small pieces until it becomes like tablets, the familiar gates. Al-Zamakhshari said: "(It will be opened so it becomes gates): that is, its gates will be many because of the descent of the angels, as if it is nothing but open gates, like His saying: ﴿And We caused the earth to burst forth with springs﴾ [al-Qamar: 12], as if all of it were springs gushing forth." It was also said: the gates are the roads and paths, meaning it will be removed and the place will open up and become roads that nothing can block. ﴿So it will become a mirage (sarab)﴾: that is, it will become something like nothing, due to the scattering of its parts and the dispersal of its substances. End of quotation. Ibn 'Atiyya said: it is an expression for its dissolving and perishing after becoming scattered dust, and he did not intend that the mountains resemble water to a viewer at a distance. Al-Wahidi said: it is by omission of a modifier, meaning "possessing gates."

Commentary of Abu Hayyan (al-Bahr al-Muhit) on surah 78, verse 21–40 (part 1 of 2):

His saying, Exalted and Majestic is He: (p-413) ﴿Indeed, Hell has been a lookout,﴾ ﴿a dwelling place for the transgressors,﴾ ﴿remaining therein for ages.﴾ ﴿They will not taste therein any coolness or drink,﴾ ﴿except scalding water and dark, cold liquid,﴾ ﴿as a recompense, fitting.﴾ ﴿Indeed, they used not to expect any reckoning,﴾ ﴿and they denied Our signs with [great] denial.﴾ ﴿And We have enumerated all things in writing.﴾ ﴿So taste [this], for We will not increase you except in torment.﴾ ﴿Indeed, for the righteous is a place of success:﴾ ﴿gardens and grapevines,﴾ ﴿and full-breasted companions of equal age,﴾ ﴿and a full cup.﴾ ﴿They will not hear therein any idle talk or lying,﴾ ﴿as a reward from your Lord, a gift [in full] calculated,﴾ ﴿Lord of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them, the Most Merciful; they will not be able to address Him,﴾ ﴿the Day the Spirit and the angels will stand in rows. None will speak except one whom the Most Merciful permits, and he will say what is correct.﴾ ﴿That is the Day of Truth. So whoever wills may take to his Lord a return.﴾ ﴿Indeed, We have warned you of a near punishment, the Day a man will look at what his hands have put forth, and the disbeliever will say, "Would that I were dust!"﴾.

(مِرْصادًا) (mirṣādan): a lookout. It is on the pattern mif‘āl, from al-raṣd (watching), meaning it watches over whoever the word of punishment has come due upon. Muqatil said: "a place of waiting for the enemies and a passageway for the allies." The form mif‘āl is used for both masculine and feminine without a tā’ and carries the sense of the relative (nisba), i.e., "possessing watching"; and everything that comes in reports and attributes in the sense of nisba carries the sense of intensification and permanence. Al-Azhari said: al-mirṣād is the place where the enemy is watched. Al-Hasan said: "Indeed, over Hell is a lookout: whoever comes with a passport passes, and whoever does not come with a passport is detained." Abu ‘Amr, al-Minqari and Ibn Ya‘mar read ﴿أنّ جهنم﴾ (anna jahannama) with a fatḥa on the hamza, while the majority read it with a kasra. (مَآبًا) (ma’aban): a return. ‘Abdullah, ‘Alqama, Zayd ibn ‘Ali, Ibn Thabbat, ‘Amr ibn Maymun, ‘Amr ibn Shurahbil, Talha, al-A‘mash, Hamza, Qutayba, Sawra and Rawh read ﴿لَبِثِينَ﴾ (labithina) without an alif after the lam, while the majority read it with an alif after it. Fā‘il indicates one in whom the act has occurred, and fa‘il indicates one whose nature is that, like ḥādhir and ḥadhir. (أحْقابًا) (aḥqāban): its discussion has preceded in al-Kahf at His saying: ﴿أو أمضي حقبا﴾ [al-Kahf: 60]. The meaning here is: age after age, each age followed by another without end. The word ḥuqub is used only where the succession of times is intended, as in the verse of Abu Tammam:
"Indeed, the ages have taken from the abode of Mawiyya, the ages that wear down the abandoned places, or are they plundered?"

It is permissible for ﴿للطاغين﴾ (lil-ṭāghīna) to be connected to ﴿مرصادا﴾, and it is permissible for it to be connected to (ma’aban). ﴿لابثين﴾ (lābithīna) is a ḥāl (circumstantial accusative) from ﴿الطاغين﴾, and ﴿أحقابا﴾ is in the accusative as an adverb of time. Al-Zamakhshari said: there is another possibility, that it be from ḥaqiba ‘āmunā when its rain and goodness diminish, and ḥaqiba when one misses sustenance, so he is ḥaqib, and its plural is aḥqāb, so it is accusative as a ḥāl concerning them, meaning: remaining therein, ḥaqibīn, jaḥidīn (deprived and denying).

His saying: ﴿لا يذوقون فيها بردا ولا شرابا﴾ (They will not taste therein any coolness or drink) is an explanation of it, and the exception is disjunctive, meaning: they will not taste therein any coolness or refreshment that cools the heat of the fire for them, nor any drink that quenches their thirst; rather, they will taste therein ﴿حميمًا وغسّاقا﴾ (scalding water and dark, cold liquid). End of quote. He had put forward before this view the following text: "It is possible that what is meant is: remaining therein for ages, not tasting coolness or drink except scalding water and dark liquid, then after the ages they will be given in exchange something other than the scalding water and dark liquid, of another kind of punishment." End of quote. This view (p-414) which he stated is an opinion of the earlier scholars, related by Ibn ‘Atiyya. He said: Others said the meaning is: remaining therein for ages, not tasting coolness or drink; in this state they will remain for ages, and then the punishment will continue everlastingly while they drink the drinks of Hell. What appears is that His saying ﴿لا يذوقون﴾ is a new independent sentence and not in the position of a ḥāl, and ﴿إلا حميمًا﴾ is a connected exception from His saying ﴿ولا شرابا﴾, and that ﴿أحقابا﴾ is in the accusative as an adverb of time, following the well-known usage of the Arabic language, not as an accusative of ḥāl according to that less well-known dialect. The saying of whoever said that those described as abiding for ages are the disobedient believers is refuted by the endings of the verses. Muqatil's saying that this is abrogated by His saying ﴿فذوقوا فلن نزيدكم إلا عذابا﴾ is corrupt. The apparent meaning, which is the view of the majority, is that coolness (bard) is the touch of cold air, that is, nothing touches them from it that is pleasant and breaks the intensity of the heat. Abu ‘Ubayda, al-Kisa’i, al-Fadl ibn Khalid and Mu‘adh al-Nahwi said: bard here means sleep, and the Arabs call it that because it cools the blaze of thirst. From their speech: "Sleep prevented coolness (bard) from cooling." The poet said:
"If you wished, I would forbid women other than you, and if you wished, I would not taste nuqakh or bard (sleep)."
Al-Nuqakh is water, and bard is sleep. In the book Lughat fi'l-Qur'an it is stated that bard is sleep in the dialect of Hudhayl. On these two views the tasting is figurative. Ibn ‘Abbas said: bard is cold, delicious drink, and from it is the saying of Hassan ibn Thabit:
"They give to drink whoever comes to al-Barisa among them, coolness mixed with a flowing, sealed wine."
And from it is the saying of another:
"Sweet longings from Su‘da, as if Su‘da had given you to drink of them, coolness, when you were thirsty."
On this view, the tasting is literal. The grammarians recite on this view the verse of Hassan: Baradā, with a fatḥa on the rā’ and the dāl, followed by the feminine alif, which is a river in Damascus. The explanation of ḥamīm and ghassāq has already been given, and the readers' difference concerning the shadda and the lightness of the shīn. (وِفاقًا) (wifāqan): that is, corresponding to their deeds and their disbelief. The recompense is described by a verbal noun of wāfaqa, or by omitting a modifier, meaning: possessing correspondence. Al-Farra’ said: it is the plural of wifq. The majority read with a light fā’, while Abu Haywa, Abu Bahriyya and Ibn Abi ‘Abla read it with a shadda, from waffaqahu kadhā. (لا يرجون) (lā yarjūna): they do not fear, or they do not believe. Expecting and hoping are different, and the meaning here is: they do not affirm reckoning, so they neither believe nor fear. The majority read (كِذّابًا) (kidhdhāban) with a shadda on the dhāl, the verbal noun of kadhdhaba, and this is a dialect of some Yemeni Arabs who make the verbal noun of fa‘ala as fi‘āl, while others make its verbal noun on the pattern tafʿīl, like taktheeb. From that dialect is the saying of the poet:
"Indeed, it has long hindered me from my companions, and from a need whose fulfilment is from my healing."
And from the speech of one of them when he sought a legal ruling: "Is shaving better for you or shortening?" He meant trimming, that is in the Hajj. Al-Zamakhshari said: fi‘āl in the pattern fa‘ala is common in the speech of the eloquent Arabs, who say nothing else; one of them heard me explaining a verse and said: "You have explained it with fisār (explanation), such as has never been heard." ‘Ali, ‘Awf al-A‘rabi, Abu Raja’, al-A‘mash and ‘Isa, with a variant from him, read it with a light dhāl. The companion of al-Lawāmiḥ said: ‘Ali and ‘Isa of Basra and ‘Awf al-A‘rabi: (kidhāban), both with lightness, and that is the dialect of Yemen, by making the verbal noun of kadhiba light, kidhāban, like kataba kitāban, so the verbal noun here carries the meaning of the verb rather than its form, like u‘tīhi ‘aṭā’an. End of quote. Al-A‘sha said:
"So I confirmed her and I denied her, and a man benefits from his lying."

End of quote. The first grammatical analysis is the more apparent, and anything else is far-fetched. In the book of Ibn ‘Atiyya and the book of al-Lawāmiḥ: ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar ibn ‘Abd al-‘Aziz read, and in the book of Ibn Khalawayh: ‘Umar ibn ‘Abd al-‘Aziz and al-Majishun; then they agreed on (كُذّابًا) (kuddhāban) with a ḍamma on the kāf and a shadda on the dhāl. The majority read ﴿وكل شيء﴾ (wa kulla shay’) in the accusative, while Abu al-Sammal read it in the nominative. (كِتابًا) (kitāban) is in the accusative as a verbal noun from the meaning of (aḥṣaynāhu), that is, an enumeration; or (aḥṣaynāhu) carries the meaning of (katabnāhu), and the figurative usage is either in the verbal noun or in the verb, because they meet in the meaning of recording; or it is a verbal noun in the position of a ḥāl, or written in the Preserved Tablet and in the scroll of the recording angels. ﴿وكل شيء﴾ is a general term with a specific sense, meaning: every thing that is subject to reward and punishment; and it is a parenthetical sentence. ﴿فذوقوا﴾ (fa-dhūqū) is a consequence of their disbelief in the reckoning, and so of their denial of the signs.

‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar said: No verse was revealed concerning the people of the Fire more severe than this one. Abu Burda related it from the Prophet (ﷺ). When He mentioned some of the state of the people of the Fire, He mentioned what is for the people of Paradise, saying: ﴿إن للمتقين مفازا﴾ (Indeed, for the righteous is a place of success), that is, a place of triumph and victory, where they were removed from the Fire and admitted into Paradise. (حدائق) (ḥadā'iqa) is a substitute for ﴿مفازا﴾ and for (fawzan), so the substance (jirm) substitutes for the meaning with an omission, meaning: the triumph of gardens, that is, by them. (دهاقا) (dihāqan): the majority said: overflowing. Mujahid and Ibn Jubayr said: consecutive. End of quote. So its meaning is maḥsib, that is, sufficient. Ibn ‘Abbas and Sarah read ḥasanan with an nūn, from al-husn (goodness). Al-Mahdawi related from him ḥasban with a fatḥa on the ḥā’ and a sukūn on the sīn and the bā’, like your saying: ḥasbuka kadhā, that is, sufficient for you.

Abu Hayyan's commentary (al-Bahr al-Muhit) on Surah 78, verses 21–40 (part 2 of 2):

Abdullah (ibn Mas'ud), Ibn Abi Ishaq, al-A'mash, Ibn Muhaysin, Ibn 'Amir and 'Asim read (rabbi, wa-l-Rahmani) with the genitive case (jarr) on both. Al-A'raj, Abu Ja'far, Shayba, Abu 'Amr and the two Haramis read both with the nominative (raf'), while al-Akhawan (Hamza and al-Kisa'i) read (rabbi) in the genitive and (al-Rahmanu) in the nominative. This is the reading of al-Hasan, Ibn Thabit, al-A'mash, and Ibn Muhaysin, with a variant transmitted from the latter two regarding the genitive, as a substitution (badal) from ﴿rabbika﴾. (Al-Rahman) is either an attribute (sifa), or a substitute (badal) from (rabb), or an appositive ('atf bayan). Whether it can be a substitute from ﴿rabbika﴾ is open to question, because an apparent substitute is not repeated, so it would function like the attributes. The nominative is either by supposing (huwa rabbu, "He is the Lord"), or as a new subject (ibtida'), with its predicate being ﴿la yamlikun﴾. The pronoun in ﴿la yamlikun﴾ refers to the polytheists, as said by 'Ata' from Ibn 'Abbas, meaning that the polytheists do not address God; as for the believers, they intercede and God accepts that from them. It is also said that it refers to the believers, meaning they do not have the power to address Him concerning any matter, because they know that whatever He does is just. It is also said that it refers to the inhabitants of the heavens and the earth, and the pronoun in ﴿minhu﴾ refers to Him, Exalted, and the meaning is that they do not have the power, from God, to address Him concerning anything of reward and punishment with an address by which they could dispose of it as owners do, adding to it or subtracting from it.

The governing element of (yawma) is either ﴿la yamlikun﴾ or ﴿la yatakallamun﴾. The disagreement about (al-Ruh) has already been mentioned: is it Gabriel, or the greatest of the angels in creation, or a creation in the form of the children of Adam, or a creation that guards the angels, or the spirits of the children of Adam, or the Qur'an and its standing? (Qiyam here) is a metaphor, meaning the manifestation of its effects resulting from its confirmation or denial. The apparent reading is that the pronoun in ﴿la yatakallamun﴾ refers to ﴿al-Ruh wa-l-mala'ikah﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said it refers to the people, so no one speaks except by permission from Him, Exalted, and he speaks what is right. 'Ikrimah said: "what is right" is "there is no god but God," meaning he said it in this world. Al-Zamakhshari said: these are two conditions: that the speaker among them be permitted to speak, and that he speak what is right, so he does not intercede for anyone who is not approved, based on His saying, Exalted: ﴿And they do not intercede except for those whom He approves﴾ [al-Anbiya: 28]. End of quotation.

﴿That is the true day﴾, meaning its existence and occurrence. ﴿So whoever wills﴾ is a warning and threat. The address in ﴿We have warned you﴾ is to those present with the Prophet (ﷺ), and whoever comes after them is included. (A punishment) is the punishment of the Hereafter, because its occurrence is certain, and everything that is coming is near. ﴿The Day when a man looks at what his hands have sent forward﴾ is general to the believer and the disbeliever, ﴿of good or evil﴾, since proof is established for him and against him. Al-Zamakhshari said, and 'Ata' said before him, that (al-mar') is the disbeliever, based on His saying: ﴿Indeed, We have warned you of a near punishment﴾, and the disbeliever is expressed by an apparent noun placed in the position of the pronoun to increase blame. The meaning of ﴿what his hands have sent forward﴾ is evil, based on His saying: ﴿Taste the punishment of the burning﴾ [al-Anfal: 50], ﴿That is for what your hands have sent forward﴾ [al-Anfal: 51]. Ibn 'Abbas, Qatadah and al-Hasan said: (al-mar') here is the believer, as if they looked at his counterpart in His saying: ﴿and the disbeliever says﴾.

The majority read (al-mar'u) with a fatha on the mim, while Ibn Abi Ishaq read it with a damma, and Abu Hatim considered this weak; it should not be considered weak, because it is a dialect in which the vowel of the mim follows the vowel of the hamza, so they say (mur'un), (mar'an), and (mir'in) according to the case endings (i'rab). (Ma) is in the accusative governed by (yandhuru), and its meaning is: he awaits what his hands have sent forward; so (ma) is a relative pronoun. It is also permissible that (yandhuru) be from looking (al-nazar), and it is suspended from the clause, so it is in the position of the accusative by supposing the removal of the preposition. (Ma) is an interrogative, in the accusative, as previously mentioned; and his wish for that is, that he be dust in this world and was never created, or on that day. Abu Hurayrah and Abdullah ibn 'Umar said: God, Exalted, brings the animals on the Day of Resurrection and takes retribution from some of them for others, then says to them after that: "Be dust," and all of them become dust. So when the disbeliever sees that, he wishes for the same. It is also said: the disbeliever here is Iblis, who, when he sees what the believers obtain of reward, says: ﴿O, would that I were dust﴾, like Adam, who was created from dust, and whom he had despised at first. It is also said: (turaban) means humble in obedience to God, Exalted, neither tyrannical nor arrogant.

Commentary of Abu Hayyan (al-Bahr al-Muhit) on surah 78, verse 21–40 (part 1 of 2):

His saying, Exalted and Majestic is He: (p-413) ﴿Indeed, Hell has been a lookout,﴾ ﴿a dwelling place for the transgressors,﴾ ﴿remaining therein for ages.﴾ ﴿They will not taste therein any coolness or drink,﴾ ﴿except scalding water and dark, cold liquid,﴾ ﴿as a recompense, fitting.﴾ ﴿Indeed, they used not to expect any reckoning,﴾ ﴿and they denied Our signs with [great] denial.﴾ ﴿And We have enumerated all things in writing.﴾ ﴿So taste [this], for We will not increase you except in torment.﴾ ﴿Indeed, for the righteous is a place of success:﴾ ﴿gardens and grapevines,﴾ ﴿and full-breasted companions of equal age,﴾ ﴿and a full cup.﴾ ﴿They will not hear therein any idle talk or lying,﴾ ﴿as a reward from your Lord, a gift [in full] calculated,﴾ ﴿Lord of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them, the Most Merciful; they will not be able to address Him,﴾ ﴿the Day the Spirit and the angels will stand in rows. None will speak except one whom the Most Merciful permits, and he will say what is correct.﴾ ﴿That is the Day of Truth. So whoever wills may take to his Lord a return.﴾ ﴿Indeed, We have warned you of a near punishment, the Day a man will look at what his hands have put forth, and the disbeliever will say, "Would that I were dust!"﴾.

(مِرْصادًا) (mirṣādan): a lookout. It is on the pattern mif‘āl, from al-raṣd (watching), meaning it watches over whoever the word of punishment has come due upon. Muqatil said: "a place of waiting for the enemies and a passageway for the allies." The form mif‘āl is used for both masculine and feminine without a tā’ and carries the sense of the relative (nisba), i.e., "possessing watching"; and everything that comes in reports and attributes in the sense of nisba carries the sense of intensification and permanence. Al-Azhari said: al-mirṣād is the place where the enemy is watched. Al-Hasan said: "Indeed, over Hell is a lookout: whoever comes with a passport passes, and whoever does not come with a passport is detained." Abu ‘Amr, al-Minqari and Ibn Ya‘mar read ﴿أنّ جهنم﴾ (anna jahannama) with a fatḥa on the hamza, while the majority read it with a kasra. (مَآبًا) (ma’aban): a return. ‘Abdullah, ‘Alqama, Zayd ibn ‘Ali, Ibn Thabbat, ‘Amr ibn Maymun, ‘Amr ibn Shurahbil, Talha, al-A‘mash, Hamza, Qutayba, Sawra and Rawh read ﴿لَبِثِينَ﴾ (labithina) without an alif after the lam, while the majority read it with an alif after it. Fā‘il indicates one in whom the act has occurred, and fa‘il indicates one whose nature is that, like ḥādhir and ḥadhir. (أحْقابًا) (aḥqāban): its discussion has preceded in al-Kahf at His saying: ﴿أو أمضي حقبا﴾ [al-Kahf: 60]. The meaning here is: age after age, each age followed by another without end. The word ḥuqub is used only where the succession of times is intended, as in the verse of Abu Tammam:
"Indeed, the ages have taken from the abode of Mawiyya, the ages that wear down the abandoned places, or are they plundered?"

It is permissible for ﴿للطاغين﴾ (lil-ṭāghīna) to be connected to ﴿مرصادا﴾, and it is permissible for it to be connected to (ma’aban). ﴿لابثين﴾ (lābithīna) is a ḥāl (circumstantial accusative) from ﴿الطاغين﴾, and ﴿أحقابا﴾ is in the accusative as an adverb of time. Al-Zamakhshari said: there is another possibility, that it be from ḥaqiba ‘āmunā when its rain and goodness diminish, and ḥaqiba when one misses sustenance, so he is ḥaqib, and its plural is aḥqāb, so it is accusative as a ḥāl concerning them, meaning: remaining therein, ḥaqibīn, jaḥidīn (deprived and denying).

His saying: ﴿لا يذوقون فيها بردا ولا شرابا﴾ (They will not taste therein any coolness or drink) is an explanation of it, and the exception is disjunctive, meaning: they will not taste therein any coolness or refreshment that cools the heat of the fire for them, nor any drink that quenches their thirst; rather, they will taste therein ﴿حميمًا وغسّاقا﴾ (scalding water and dark, cold liquid). End of quote. He had put forward before this view the following text: "It is possible that what is meant is: remaining therein for ages, not tasting coolness or drink except scalding water and dark liquid, then after the ages they will be given in exchange something other than the scalding water and dark liquid, of another kind of punishment." End of quote. This view (p-414) which he stated is an opinion of the earlier scholars, related by Ibn ‘Atiyya. He said: Others said the meaning is: remaining therein for ages, not tasting coolness or drink; in this state they will remain for ages, and then the punishment will continue everlastingly while they drink the drinks of Hell. What appears is that His saying ﴿لا يذوقون﴾ is a new independent sentence and not in the position of a ḥāl, and ﴿إلا حميمًا﴾ is a connected exception from His saying ﴿ولا شرابا﴾, and that ﴿أحقابا﴾ is in the accusative as an adverb of time, following the well-known usage of the Arabic language, not as an accusative of ḥāl according to that less well-known dialect. The saying of whoever said that those described as abiding for ages are the disobedient believers is refuted by the endings of the verses. Muqatil's saying that this is abrogated by His saying ﴿فذوقوا فلن نزيدكم إلا عذابا﴾ is corrupt. Abu ‘Ubayda, al-Kisa’i, al-Fadl ibn Khalid and Mu‘adh al-Nahwi said: bard here means sleep, and the Arabs call it that because it cools the blaze of thirst. From their speech: "Sleep prevented coolness (bard) from cooling." The poet said:
"If you wished, I would forbid women other than you, and if you wished, I would not taste nuqakh or bard (sleep)."
